research_rationale: EO 11600 (36 FR 12471, Federal Register of July 1, 1971, signed June 29, 1971; held official Federal Register text) is a single approval: the President approves a seal of office for the Office of Management and Budget, the design of which is made part of the order. The order has no duration, condition, report date, delegation or revocation language of its own, so it has no own-terms end. The held corpus contains no later instrument that names EO 11600: the dossier's later-event chain is empty and the three bounded machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) report no hits for this order; a cross-corpus search for the number and for the order's approval wording found only the order's own copies, the 1989 OFR codification snapshot (editorial, not used as the current basis) and an unrelated index. Coverage notes read: the U.S. Code search covers release point 119-121 current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected); the eCFR search is a point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14; the later-events search covers Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences in saved order texts. The established original_plus_bounded_search route is used for the YES: held original, no later event, no own-terms end, no hit in the searches. A formal revocation could not be shown, so the order is unrevoked on the held record.
savings_reason: The order has no savings, transition or residual provision and nothing in it was terminated, so no savings question arises. The bounded searches found no later instrument that could have ended the approval or preserved a residue of it.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held corpus by number and by the approval wording for an earlier revocation, supersession, replacement seal or own-terms end; none exists in held texts, and the order states no date, condition or duration. The 1989 OFR codification entry lists the order as in force but is editorial and is not relied on as a current basis.
scope_check: Complete inventory is one operative paragraph: the approval of the seal (the order's recital of the Director's recommendation and the design description are not separate commands). The dossier inventory has exactly this one clause and it covers the whole operative text.
independent_command_check: There is one command only, the approval of the seal as the official seal of the Office of Management and Budget; it is a standing designation, not a one-time performance that is exhausted, because the seal remains the office's official seal until changed by a later approval, and none is held.
savings_check: No savings or accrued-rights language; none_after_bounded_search with the original as the cited source.

research_rationale: EO 11961 (42 FR 4321, Federal Register of January 24, 1977, signed January 19, 1977; held official Federal Register text, filed 1-20-77) delegates to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget the President's functions under the International Investment Survey Act of 1976 (22 U.S.C. 3101) and, in the absence of a contrary delegation or direction by the Director, assigns particular functions to the Secretary of the Treasury (portfolio investment), the Secretary of Commerce (direct investment) and, originally, the Council on International Economic Policy (periodic reports to Congress). Later instruments: EO 12013 (42 FR 54931, effective October 9, 1977) amended section 4; EO 12318 (46 FR 42833, effective August 23, 1981) revoked EO 12013 and further amended section 4; EO 12518 (50 FR 23661, signed June 3, 1985) redesignated the order as International Investment and Trade in Services, substituted the new statute name and amended sections 2 and 3. Each is an amendment under the strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21, so each is recorded as a later event and the clause continues as amended; none revokes or supersedes the order, and the official Federal Register texts of all three are held. Bounded searches were read through their coverage notes: current-law:usc (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected) has 10 hits, of which the lead of record is that the U.S. Code prints the order, as amended by EOs 12013, 12318 and 12518, as a note to 22 U.S.C. 3101 with no ending statement, and 22 U.S.C. 3141 names the order; current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) has 10 hits that are authority and purpose citations of the order in Treasury and Commerce survey regulations; later-events:ofr_catalog has 5 hits, all the three amendments above. No revocation, supersession or own-terms end was found. The established original_plus_bounded_search route supports the YES. The dossier inventory split the order wrongly (section 3 had been merged into section 2 and its tail listed as a separate item), so the inventory is corrected to the four sections 1-4 by absolute offsets in the registered Federal Register text.
savings_reason: Nothing in the order ended, so no residue is created; the delegations and assignments continue as amended. The bounded searches found no later instrument that ended or preserved a residue of any section.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held corpus for the number EO 11961 (12 citing texts listed in the packet lookups): the citing orders are EO 12013, EO 12318 and EO 12518 (all amendments), the 1989 OFR codification, and current regulation and Code texts that cite the order as authority. None revokes, supersedes or ends it. EO 12013 itself was revoked by EO 12318 section 4(a), but that revocation did not remove the order or its section 4; EO 12318 section 4(b) re-amended section 4.
scope_check: Four operative sections: 1 (delegation to the OMB Director, with power to designate others), 2 (Treasury, portfolio investment), 3 (Commerce, direct investment) and 4 (periodic reports to Congress). The dossier's section-2 span had absorbed section 3 and left its tail as a stray item, so the inventory is corrected; the enacting recital is not a command. The conditions in sections 2-4 that the assignment applies in the absence of any contrary delegation or direction by the Director are conditions on the assignment, not ends: no contrary Director direction is held that would end an assignment.
independent_command_check: Section 1 (delegation of all the President's functions under the Act to the Director) is independent of sections 2-4, which are default assignments subordinate to it. Section 4's CIEP assignment was replaced by EO 12013 (to the Secretary of Commerce, 4(a)(3) and 5(c) of the Act) and then EO 12318 (Secretary of Commerce, periodic reports under 4(a)(3)); this strike-and-insert is an amendment, not an end of the command.
savings_check: No savings clause and no ended clause; savings state none_after_bounded_search with the original as the source.

research_rationale: EO 12046 (43 FR 13349, Federal Register of March 29, 1978, signed March 27, 1978, filed 3-28-78; held official Federal Register text, jobs/fr-originals) implements Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1977 by moving the functions of the Office of Telecommunications Policy (OTP): frequency assignment, satellite, spectrum and policy functions to the Secretary of Commerce (section 2), procurement and frequency-appeals functions to the OMB Director (section 3), emergency and National Communications System functions to the President, with the NSC and OSTP (section 4), related functions of Commerce, State and GSA (section 5), and transition, amendment and general provisions (section 6, effective March 26, 1978). Attempt 1 held this order for effort gaps. Reading the order in full, the dossier's 26 machine scopes were span-based and overlapping (three duplicated segments; sec2-i absorbed 2-4 to 2-5; sec4 absorbed 4-1 to 4-3), so the inventory is corrected to 25 paragraph-aligned scopes, which lets each revoked paragraph carry its own end. Later instruments that name EO 12046: EO 12127 (1979) only recites it when moving Emergency Broadcast System functions to the Federal Emergency Management Agency; EO 12148 (effective July 15, 1979) amended section 5-3; EO 12472 (effective on Federal Register publication, April 5, 1984) revoked sections 2-414, 4-102, 4-103, 4-202, 4-302, 5-3 and 6-101 and amended 2-411. Orders 12829, 13355, 13381, 13467, 13470, 13516, 13549, 13587, 13691 and 13764 are attached to the dossier as machine leads, but none contains the number 12046 (checked by search of the held texts), so none touches it; EO 13618 (2012) revokes EO 12472 as amended but does not name EO 12046. Sections 1-1 and 6-2 are self-executing implementation and conforming commands exhausted on the order's own effective date; the revoked sections end on EO 12472's effective date; the remaining sections are standing allocations with no ending event and a current predicate through 2026-10-14 (47 U.S.C. 901(b)(6) and 47 CFR 213.0 treat the order as operative). So the order is 'yes': formally unrevoked, with most operative sections continuing. Savings: the transfers made by sections 1 and 6 and the functions reassigned by EO 12472 survive as effects.
savings_reason: Sections 1-1 and 6-2 were exhausted by performance on March 26, 1978, but the transfers, the abolition of the Office of Telecommunications Policy and the revocation of EOs 10705, 11191 and 11556 that they carried out are accrued effects; the functions of the sections revoked by EO 12472 (2-414, 4-102, 4-103, 4-202, 4-302, 5-3, 6-101) were reassigned by that order, which records them as 'assignments of responsibility provided by this Order'. The sections not revoked continue, so they leave no residue. No separate savings clause was found in the order or in EO 12472.
conflict_resolutions: {"PARTIAL_END_CANDIDATE_ON_YES_ORDER": "EO 12472 section 4(b)(1) revokes only sections 2-414, 4-102, 4-103, 4-202, 4-302, 5-3 and 6-101 of EO 12046 as amended, and 4(b)(3) amends 2-411; the revocation is partial and does not end the order. The machine lead that lists scopes 2-101 to 2-502 (except 2-414) as revoked misreads the section 2 heading in the revocation sentence: the held text of EO 12472 names section 2-414 alone from section 2. Each revoked section is therefore recorded terminated with its own end (effective April 5, 1984), and the other sections stay operative; the order as a whole remains in force (status yes)."}
earlier_end_check: Searched the held corpus for the number 12046 (cruden search over every held text, plus the dossier's 16 citing texts): the orders naming it are EO 12127 (recital only), EO 12148 (amends 5-3) and EO 12472 (revokes seven sections, amends 2-411), plus the 1989 codification, current USC/CFR texts and the Code notes. The machine leads EO 12829, 13355, 13381, 13467, 13470, 13516, 13549, 13587, 13691 and 13764 do not contain the number 12046. No earlier revocation, supersession or own-terms end of any scope was found; each revoked section's end is the express revocation by EO 12472 (effective April 5, 1984), and the two self-executing scopes end on the order's effective date. EO 13618 (2012) revoked EO 12472 but does not name EO 12046 and cannot revive the revoked sections.
scope_check: 25 corrected scopes in order: 1-1 (implementation, performed); 1-2 (recital of allocation); 2-1, 2-2, 2-3 (Commerce functions); 2-4 (2-401 to 2-410); 2-411 (amended); 2-412/2-413; 2-414 (revoked); 2-5; 3 (OMB); 4-101; 4-102 and 4-103 (revoked); 4-2 (4-201); 4-202 (revoked); 4-3 (4-301); 4-302 (revoked); 5-1; 5-2; 5-3 (amended, then revoked); 6-101 (revoked); 6-102 to 6-104; 6-2 (performed); 6-3 (agency directions, limits and effective date). The enacting recital is not a command. Contiguous offsets from the registered text cover section 1 to the effective-date sentence.
independent_command_check: Each scope is an independent command: the revocation of 2-414, 4-102, 4-103, 4-202, 4-302, 5-3 or 6-101 does not touch the sibling sections 4-101, 4-201 and 4-301 or the Commerce sections 2-1 to 2-5. EO 12472's supersession of the 1963 Memorandum is disclosed on 4-201 but no source shows it extinguished the transfer to the President. 5-3 had a strike-and-insert amendment by EO 12148 (a later event) before its revocation; 2-411 was amended by EO 12472 and continues.
savings_check: Savings state transferred_or_accrued from the order itself: the accrued transfers of sections 1 and 6, and the functions reassigned by EO 12472 for the revoked sections. Not an end of any command.
